## Historical audit — S0079, chunk 2 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_regression_guidance/C1/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Only the supplied chunk was examined; neither referenced image is visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Line 12, `model_request`, chars [0,177941) | The task explicitly requested a 3D reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, including camera and framing. The student’s inventory interpreted it as a paneled room with a chaise, pillow, label, curtain, parquet, and cropped cane chair. This inventory is the student’s interpretation, not independent image verification. |
| Line 12, same range | The first complete program constructed multiple semantic groups and separate parts, striped upholstery and wood/cane materials, a tilted pillow, camera, and lights. It claimed contacts and parenting; these are construction choices, not proof of geometric connection or visible coverage. Step 1 timed out after about 600 seconds with empty stdout and stderr: a **technical interruption**, with no observable render and no established cause. |
| Line 12, same range | In response to the failure, the student batched parquet and cane, reduced mesh detail and samples, and retained the principal scene groups. Step 2 reported `ok: true` and a saved render. The runner then requested comparison of framing, coverage and contacts. The reference and render were supplied to the next student session; line 13 confirms two image inputs and zero tool calls. |
| Line 14, student `model_response`, chars [0,16258); line 15, `execute`, chars [0,16971) | The student reported stronger diagonal wall and seat edges in the successful image and hypothesized excessive camera displacement toward the foot. It executed a more frontal camera position and changed target and lens, expecting flatter edges and greater head-panel exposure, while retaining the scene construction. This is a student diagnosis and test, not an independently verified visual finding. |
| Line 16, `execution_result`, chars [0,132460); line 17, `select`, chars [0,59) | Step 3 reported `ok: true`, finished rendering, saved an image and blend file, and was selected. This is **formal execution success**, not proof of reconstruction accuracy. |

**Guidance and exploration.** The visible inputs contain task/system procedure and runner feedback, including the timeout-repair instruction and post-render review prompt. No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student receipt is shown in this chunk. The student’s batching repair and camera hypothesis are visible autonomous choices within that guidance; the camera program was actually executed.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Batching repeated geometry was followed by a successful run, but the timeout’s cause was not isolated; the specific chaise inventory, landmarks and camera values are task-specific. The student’s camera hypothesis remains unresolved here: no independent comparison of the two renders, support contacts, part connections, object visibility, materials, lighting or pose is available. The selected step’s visual correctness and the outcome outside this chunk are unknown.
